title: MercadoLibre and Dutch Bros Have Fallen More Than 30% From Their Record Highs. Here's Why Both Are Worth Buying Now.
detail:
MercadoLibre and Dutch Bros Have Fallen More Than 30% From Their Record Highs. Here's Why Both Are Worth Buying Now.
Jennifer Saibil, The Motley Fool
Sun, November 1, 2026 at 4:50 AM CST 5 min read
MELI
BROS
^GSPC
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The S&P 500 is hitting new highs, but that doesn't mean every great stock is soaring this year. There are all kinds of reasons a top stock could move down in a strong bull market, and sometimes, that creates investing opportunities.

Consider MercadoLibre (NASDAQ: MELI) and Dutch Bros (NYSE: BROS). Both of these stocks have incredible long-term potential, but they're 37% and 49% off their highs, respectively. Here's why you should buy them on the dip.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.
1. MercadoLibre: 37% off highs

MercadoLibre is a Latin American e-commerce superstar. It operates in 18 countries in the region, with a complete platform including logistics, media, and a payments business. Its payments and media businesses have actually become major growth drivers on their own, and the ecosystem puts MercadoLibre in an excellent position to benefit from the shift to digital in Latin America.

It's the largest e-commerce company in its region, and it's building what it expects to be the biggest digital bank in the area as well. It has the most comprehensive logistics program, with 77% of shipments (not chosen to be slow) delivered within 48 hours. Management sees the company's edge in its ecosystem, as artificial intelligence provides consumer recommendations and informs accurate digital ads, and customers on the platform can easily pay through the payments system. That even leads to more users buying insurance policies through the financial platform.

There are 670 million people in Latin America who make up MercadoLibre's addressable market, and the median age is a decade younger than in the U.S. and China. They are also highly connected digitally, even though they lag other regions in e-commerce and digital banking penetration.

MercadoLibre consistently reports high growth, including a 50% increase in revenue year over year in the second quarter, a 56% increase in total payment volume, and a 44% increase in gross merchandise volume.

The stock is down right now because profitability has declined for the past two quarters. Management says it needs to invest to build and grow more, but the market was disappointed.

As soon as profitability starts to increase, the price could go right back up, which is why now is the right time to buy.

2. Dutch Bros: 49% off highs

MercadoLibre Sinks 10% in a Week After Lula's Surprise Win, With Earnings Up Next ©Tevarak Phanduang from Achira22's Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

MercadoLibre stock fell 10% in a week, mostly on Monday, after Lula's surprise win in Brazil's runoff sank Brazilian stocks, Nu Holdings among them.

The worry is currency risk: a weaker real shrinks what MercadoLibre's Brazilian sales are worth in dollars.

Citi upgraded the stock to Buy after the drop, though it trimmed its target.

Third-quarter results on Nov. 4 will show whether operating margin has stopped shrinking.

MercadoLibre (MELI:NASDAQ) stock is down 10% in the past week. Most of the drop came on Monday, the first trading day after President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Brazil's runoff. Nu Holdings (NU:NYSE) fell 22% before the open that morning.

Nu had more riding on Brazil: almost 118 million of its 139 million customers are there. MercadoLibre is more spread out. Brazil was 52.6% of its 2025 revenue, Mexico 22.4% and Argentina 20.6%. Investors sold it like a Brazil stock anyway.

Investors Bet on the Wrong Candidate

Lula beat Flávio Bolsonaro 51.8% to 48.2% on Oct. 25, weeks after losing the first round. Investors had bet on a market-friendly Bolsonaro win.

Nothing in MercadoLibre's business changed over the weekend. The worry is the real: a weaker one shrinks what its Brazilian sales are worth in dollars. Last quarter the real worked the other way, and Brazil's revenue grew 59% in dollars against 42% FX-neutral.

Wall Street Bought the Dip

On Tuesday, Citi upgraded MercadoLibre to Buy from Neutral, calling the selloff an entry point, though it trimmed its target to $2,050 from $2,100.

Analysts expect normalized EPS to dip to $38.26 this year, then climb to $55.89 in 2027 and $78.56 in 2028:

MELI Normalized EPS Estimates: 2024-2029 (TIKR)

The election reaches those figures mainly through the real: a weaker one trims them in dollars.

MercadoLibre's Nov. 4 Report Is About Margins

MercadoLibre reports third-quarter results on Nov. 4. In the second quarter, revenue rose 50% to $10.2 billion, but operating margin fell to 6.7% from 12.2% a year earlier. The company spent on free shipping, credit and cheaper selling fees while Shopee pushed hard in Brazil.

The quarter ended Sept. 30, before the vote, so watch two things: whether the margin holds near 6.7%, and what management says about Brazil in the fourth quarter, the first with a weaker real.

A Buy If Margins Hold

The stock traded at 40x forward earnings on Thursday. That's far below its five-year average of 63x and not far above its March low of 30x:

MELI Stock NTM P/E: 5-Year (TIKR)

Wall Street's $2,272 consensus target is 40% above Friday's close.

I'd be a buyer here if Nov. 4 shows the margin holding at 6.7% or better and management sounds steady on Brazil.

Of course, if the real keeps sliding, MercadoLibre's dollar results will take a hit in the quarters ahead, whatever happens to margins.

title: Tech Stocks Are Selling Off. Here's Why I'd Rather Own MercadoLibre Than Any "Magnificent Seven" Stock.
detail:
Tech Stocks Are Selling Off. Here's Why I'd Rather Own MercadoLibre Than Any "Magnificent Seven" Stock.
Will Healy, The Motley Fool
Sat, October 31, 2026 at 4:25 AM CDT 5 min read
MELI
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

As anyone who follows the market closely knows, tech stocks have sold off in recent weeks. While the industry delivered on technical breakthroughs and massive revenue growth for investors, rising interest rates, along with concerns about the staggering cost of artificial intelligence (AI) build-outs, weighed on those stocks.

Fortunately, investors have more options than tech and the "Magnificent Seven." In my view, the sell-off is an excellent opportunity to consider other investments. Right now, I hold and periodically add to my position in MercadoLibre (NASDAQ: MELI), and here's why.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.
Why MercadoLibre?

Indeed, one might question the choice of MercadoLibre on the surface since it is tech-adjacent. Its e-commerce and fintech platforms depend on technology, and the company has applied AI in many of its applications. Also, in one sense, it can represent a second chance for investors who missed out on Amazon, as MercadoLibre leads the e-commerce market in Latin America.

However, MercadoLibre differs from Amazon in that it is not a cloud service provider. Thus, it has not had the massive capital expenditures (capex) that have weighed on Amazon. In the first half of 2026, MercadoLibre's capex was $712 million, a tiny fraction of the $98 billion Amazon allocated over the same period.

Furthermore, while MercadoLibre has not followed Amazon into the cloud, the consumer discretionary stock has clearly evolved into a conglomerate. Addressing the economic and political challenges in Latin America appears to have inspired that move.

When Latin America was more of a cash-based society and millions could not buy online, Mercado Pago was founded to offer digital financial products to these customers. Mercado Pago went on to serve customers not buying on MercadoLibre's e-commerce site and became the top fintech company in Latin America.

MercadoLibre employed the same strategy to improve logistics. Consequently, that enterprise, Mercado Envios, brought same-day and next-day delivery to the region.

Addressing company struggles

Nonetheless, even for those who can buy into its strategy of turning adversity into opportunity, choosing MercadoLibre may sound counterintuitive. Investors have sold the stock off over the last year. The company cut margins to stave off e-commerce competition and dramatically increased the allowance for doubtful accounts (i.e., bad loans) as it aggressively expands its loan book.

Still, the margin cuts and loan book expansion are likely to dramatically increase revenues and, by extension, profits over time. Also, its past successes should suggest that Brazil's election results are unlikely to derail the company's value proposition.

Additionally, the stock plunged following the surprise reelection of Luiz Inácio Lula Da Silva, as many shareholders perceived his opponent, Flavio Bolsonaro, would have pursued a monetary policy more favorable to MercadoLibre.

Indeed, Brazil is highly critical to the company, as it accounts for about 54% of the company's revenue in the latest quarter. However, investors should recall that MercadoLibre built much of its success by turning Latin America's economic and political challenges into business opportunities, increasing the likelihood it will do so again amid the election turmoil.

MercadoLibre's financials

The company's financials highlight both the opportunity and the adversity.

In the first half of 2026, revenue of $19 billion rose by 49% from year-ago levels. Despite that increase, net income actually fell by 13% over the same period to $883 million. The aforementioned margin cuts and bad-loan expenses weighed on its profits.

Third-quarter earnings also come out on Nov. 4. Analysts are looking for a 45% yearly revenue increase, and although that could imply a slight slowdown, the company is likely to continue growing rapidly.

Also, with the pullback, MercadoLibre trades at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 45. While that may sound high compared to the S&P 500's average earnings multiple of 26, investors should remember that the company's investments in itself have reduced profits, suggesting the stock is not as overvalued as it appears.

Moreover, MercadoLibre's market cap of $85 billion is a small fraction of Amazon's at $2.7 trillion. That implies MercadoLibre may outperform the Magnificent Seven stocks, whose larger sizes usually make higher-percentage growth more difficult. That advantage suggests it might make sense to buy the dip in MercadoLibre.

Buy MercadoLibre stock

Ultimately, MercadoLibre seems to have Amazon-like growth potential and the smaller size that should help it outperform the Magnificent Seven stocks.

Latin America's challenges, most recently highlighted by Brazil's election, add to the stock's risks. Also, MercadoLibre has had to reduce profits to solidify its e-commerce and fintech business.

Nonetheless, MercadoLibre has thrived by turning adversity into opportunity and should continue to do so. Furthermore, its moves to build market share should increase profits in the long term. Thanks to its smaller size, the stock appears to be gearing up for further growth that could easily reward investors with market-beating returns.

title: Nu Holdings Slides After Brazil's Election: Is the Sell-Off Overdone?
detail:
Nu Holdings Slides After Brazil's Election: Is the Sell-Off Overdone?
Moumita C. Chattopadhyay
Fri, October 30, 2026 at 10:40 AM CDT 3 min read
NU
^BVSP
MELI
STNE
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Nu Holdings Ltd. NU suffered a political shock this week. Following Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's reelection in Brazil, its shares fell 16.95% on Oct. 26 to $12.59. The stock finished at $12.05 on Oct. 29, down 20.5% from Oct. 23.

Investors are reassessing Brazilian market risks. The Bovespa Index lost 13.9% on Oct. 26, and the real slid more than 10% against the dollar intraday. Questions about government spending and interest rates matter for Nu because Brazil accounts for most of its customers.

These market worries contrast with operating momentum. Nu generated nearly $5.9 billion in second-quarter 2026 gross revenues, a 39% currency-neutral increase, and $1.06 billion in net income. Its customer base reached 139 million, including roughly 118 million in Brazil. Continued expansion provides some support against economic pressures.

However, credit quality deserves attention. Loans overdue more than 90 days rose 35 basis points to 6.9% in the second quarter, even as earlier-stage delinquencies eased to 4.8%. Prolonged elevated interest rates could increase repayment difficulties, pushing credit losses higher and squeezing lending profitability.

Third-quarter results, tentatively expected on Nov. 12, will help investors assess whether the share-price decline reflects broader market fears or weakening fundamentals. Loan growth, financing costs, credit provisions and currency movements will be important indicators. Sustained operating growth could support a recovery, provided asset quality remains manageable.

Nu Holdings' Brazil Peers Face Credit and Currency Risks

MercadoLibre MELI faces Brazilian currency and credit risks through its Mercado Pago unit. MercadoLibre reported second-quarter 2026 payment volume of $101 billion, up 56%, while its credit portfolio exceeded $16 billion. MercadoLibre's lending expansion supports revenue growth, but Brazil's election uncertainty could increase defaults and pressure margins over coming quarters.

StoneCo STNE also faces Brazil's shifting interest-rate outlook and merchant credit risks. StoneCo's second-quarter 2026 credit portfolio reached R$3.75 billion, up 107.5% year over year, while provisions for expected credit losses increased. StoneCo's merchant-focused lending provides growth potential, although weaker business activity could raise defaults and further restrict lending profitability.

NU's Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

Shares of NU have declined 16.6% over the past six months, underperforming the broader industry and the S&P 500 composite.

Stocktwits Wall Street Wrap — Tesla, Broadcom, MercadoLibre Get Bullish Calls As Alphabet, Enphase Face Downgrades
Shivani Kumaresan
Fri, October 30, 2026 at 4:00 AM CDT 5 min read
TSLA
GOOG
MELI

Barclays upgraded Tesla to 'Overweight' on merger potential with SpaceX and Robotaxi progress.

Citi upgraded MercadoLibre to 'Buy,' viewing its recent share price drop as a buying opportunity.

Citizens downgraded Alphabet to 'Market Perform,' citing slower search growth.

Wall Street analysts issued a mixed set of stock calls this week, upgrading Tesla Inc. (TSLA), Broadcom (AVGO) and MercadoLibre (MELI) on AI-driven growth opportunities, potential deals and regional market expansion. Meanwhile, Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL, GOOG), Enphase Energy (ENPH) and Whirlpool (WHR) faced downgrades as analysts flagged slowing growth, margin pressure and intensifying competition.

Tesla's Potential SpaceX Merger Raises Optimism

Barclays upgraded Tesla stock (TSLA) to 'Overweight' from 'Equal Weight' and increased its price target to $450 from $370, implying a 12% upside potential from the stock's last close. Analyst Dan Levy pointed to a possible combination with Elon Musk's other venture, SpaceX (SPCX), that could improve prospects for Tesla's main automotive business and advance its Robotaxi operations.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

According to the firm, the potential Tesla-SpaceX transaction could create benefits through greater business integration and address ownership considerations involving Elon Musk. Last week, SpaceX and Tesla confirmed they set up independent board committees to explore closer ties between the companies, including a possible merger.

Morningstar also offered support, saying combining Tesla and SpaceX could be a smart move because their businesses complement each other. Tesla could supply batteries and solar products to SpaceX, while Grok could support its self-driving technology and humanoid robots.

Broadcom And MercadoLibre Get A Vote Of Confidence

DA Davidson turned bullish on Broadcom stock (AVGO), upgrading it to 'Buy' from 'Neutral' and lifting its price target to $400 from $350. The analyst expects Anthropic to move ahead with a public listing and secure additional funding, followed by a potential OpenAI IPO next year.

These developments could help Broadcom grow in the coming years. The analyst believes investors are underestimating the chances of these deals happening, which could give the stock an upside if they go through.

Broadcom has a close relationship with Anthropic, supplying chips, equipment, and financing for its AI infrastructure expansion. Broadcom has also agreed to provide up to $42 billion in financing to support Anthropic's spending. The deal could make Anthropic Broadcom's biggest chip-design customer next year.

MercadoLibre received a 'Buy' rating from Citi, which previously rated the stock 'Neutral'. The firm slightly lowered its price target to $2,050 from $2,100 but believes the recent decline offers an attractive buying opportunity. Citi expects the Latin American e-commerce and financial services company to expand faster than consumer markets in its operating regions. The analyst also believes high borrowing costs in Brazil could put pressure on competing businesses.

MercadoLibre stock tumbled more than 8% this week and is on track for its worst week since May, after a sharp selloff triggered by Brazil's election results. Famed investor Michael Burry said that MELI's sharp decline offered a buying opportunity.

Alphabet And Enphase Energy Face Analyst Concerns

Citizens lowered its rating on Alphabet to 'Market Perform' from 'Outperform' after its third-quarter results. The firm noted that search growth slowed from the previous quarter, even though search activity reached its highest level in five years.

The analyst sees challenges in converting search activity into advertising revenue as Google shifts toward AI-powered summaries and agent-based services. Increasing competition in the AI assistant market could make the transition more difficult. Alphabet stock is down 11% and is tracking its worst weekly performance since the COVID-19 pandemic.

Enphase Energy stock received two separate downgrades. Oppenheimer cut its rating to 'Perform' from 'Outperform' after the company missed Q3 estimates and issued a weaker-than-expected Q4 outlook.

The firm pointed to an estimated quarterly revenue base of around $200 million for Enphase's core operations. It also warned that price cuts in energy storage products are pressuring gross margins. Higher interest rates and limited adoption of alternative financing options continue to weigh on U.S. residential solar installations.

Roth Capital downgraded Enphase to 'Neutral' from 'Buy' and slashed its price target to $30 from $55. Analyst Philip Shen pointed to weak Q3 results and a disappointing Q4 forecast. The firm also plans to lower its earnings and profit margin estimates despite Enphase's strong technology and growth potential.

Whirlpool Downgraded As Competition Intensifies

Stifel lowered its rating on Whirlpool's stock to 'Sell' from 'Hold' and cut its price target to $20 from $30 following weaker Q3 results and outlook. Whirlpool's North American appliance revenue fell 8.3% to $2.50 billion as demand weakened. Operating profit dropped 44.7% to $74 million. In Latin America, appliance revenue grew 6.9% to $858 million, but operating profit declined 61.3% to $18 million.

The analyst expects the appliance maker's difficulties to deepen as it loses ground in the important U.S. market. Planned price increases to recover higher costs could further hurt demand, particularly as competitors offer incentives and consumers show limited loyalty to individual appliance brands.

So far this year, TSLA, AVGO, MELI, ENPH, GOOGL and WHR stocks have declined between 0.3% and 59%.

We believe that we offer world-class technological and commercial solutions that address the distinctive cultural and geographic challenges of operating a digital commerce platform in Latin America.

Through its fintech platform, MercadoPago, the company offers a comprehensive set of financial technology services to users of its e-commerce platform, and to users outside of its e-commerce platform. For individuals, those services include a digital account that offers a debit card, online payments, insurance, savings, investments and credit lines. For merchants, MercadoPago offers online and physical point-of-sale payments processing services as well as the digital account. While media releases or rumors about a substantial change in a company's business prospects usually make its stock 'trending' and lead to an immediate price change, there are always some fundamental facts that eventually dominate the buy-and-hold decision-making.

Earnings Estimate Revisions

Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.

Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.

MercadoLibre is expected to post earnings of $9.41 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +13.1%. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed -0.6%.

For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $38.09 points to a change of -3.3% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has changed -2.6%.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $55.19 indicates a change of +44.9% from what MercadoLibre is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed -1.5%.

Having a strong externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, offers a more conclusive picture of a stock's price direction in the near term, since it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. Due to the size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, MercadoLibre is rated Zacks Rank #4 (Sell).

Revenue Growth Forecast

Even though a company's earnings growth is arguably the best indicator of its financial health, nothing much happens if it cannot raise its revenues. It's almost impossible for a company to grow its earnings without growing its revenue for long periods. Therefore, knowing a company's potential revenue growth is crucial.

In the case of MercadoLibre, the consensus sales estimate of $10.66 billion for the current quarter points to a year-over-year change of +43.8%. The $41.74 billion and $53.98 billion estimates for the current and next fiscal years indicate changes of +44.5% and +29.3%, respectively.

Last Reported Results and Surprise History

MercadoLibre reported revenues of $10.17 billion in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +49.8%. EPS of $9.19 for the same period compares with $10.31 a year ago.

Compared to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $9.77 billion, the reported revenues represent a surprise of +4.07%. The EPS surprise was +5.75%.

Over the last four quarters, the company surpassed EPS estimates just once. The company topped consensus revenue estimates each time over this period.

Valuation

No investment decision can be efficient without considering a stock's valuation. Whether a stock's current price rightly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects is an essential determinant of its future price performance.

While comparing the current values of a company's valuation multiples, such as price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), with its own historical values helps determine whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of the reasonability of the stock's price.

The Zacks Value Style Score (part of the Zacks Style Scores system), which pays close attention to both traditional and unconventional valuation metrics to grade stocks from A to F (an A is better than a B; a B is better than a C; and so on), is pretty helpful in identifying whether a stock is overvalued, rightly valued, or temporarily undervalued.

MercadoLibre is graded C on this front, indicating that it is trading at par with its peers. Click here to see the values of some of the valuation metrics that have driven this grade.

Bottom Line

The facts discussed here and much other information on Zacks.com might help determine whether or not it's worthwhile paying attention to the market buzz about MercadoLibre. However, its Zacks Rank #4 does suggest that it may underperform the broader market in the near term.

The market expects MercadoLibre (MELI) to deliver a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when it reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. This widely-known consensus outlook is important in assessing the company's earnings picture, but a powerful factor that might influence its near-term stock price is how the actual results compare to these estimates.

The earnings report might help the stock move higher if these key numbers are better than expectations. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call will mostly determine the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations, it's worth having a handicapping insight into the odds of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This operator of an online marketplace and payments system in Latin America is expected to post quarterly earnings of $9.41 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +13.1%.

Revenues are expected to be $10.66 billion, up 43.8% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 0.62% lower over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts may not always get reflected in the aggregate change.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise Chart for MELI
Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. Our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) -- has this insight at its core.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for MercadoLibre?

For MercadoLibre, the Most Accurate Estimate is higher than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bullish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of +4.93%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #4.

So, this combination makes it difficult to conclusively predict that MercadoLibre will beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

Analysts often consider to what extent a company has been able to match consensus estimates in the past while calculating their estimates for its future earnings. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that MercadoLibre would post earnings of $8.69 per share when it actually produced earnings of $9.19, delivering a surprise of +5.75%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates just once.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

MercadoLibre doesn't appear a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.
